name: mytrima-platform
description: Mytrima SaaS platform — NestJS application shell per Technical Master Plan v1.2, Section 4

notes.history: This was originally a dependency-free tsx + node:test scaffold, because the sandbox it was first authored in had no npm registry access. That constraint does not apply to every environment running this repo — once real registry access was confirmed, this was migrated to an actual NestJS app per Master Plan Section 4's recommendation, exactly as the earlier README said to do 'when a real engineering environment with registry access exists.'
notes.hand_rolled_crypto_kept_deliberately: auth/password.ts, auth/jwt.ts, and auth/totp.ts still use Node's built-in crypto instead of bcrypt/jsonwebtoken/otplib. That was never about registry access — it's a real, defensible dependency-count choice (see the comments in those files) — so it carried over unchanged into this migration rather than being swapped out just because dependencies are now easy to add.
notes.nestjs_v11_not_v12: Pinned to NestJS v11.x, not the newer v12.x, on purpose: v12 shipped as ESM-only ('type': 'module', no CommonJS build at all), which would force this whole codebase onto ESM (package.json 'type':'module', explicit .js extensions on every relative import under NodeNext resolution, an ESM-aware Jest setup) for no functional benefit at pilot stage. v11.x still ships plain CommonJS and is fully current and supported — this is a deliberate compatibility choice, not staleness. Revisit when the team is ready to take on an ESM migration project in its own right, not as a side effect of a routine dependency bump.
notes.bullmq_is_a_real_dependency_not_a_stub: Master Plan Section 4 names Redis/BullMQ specifically for the Automation & Notification Engine's job queue — unlike jwt/totp/password (hand-rolled deliberately), there is no reasonable hand-rolled substitute for a real job queue with retry/backoff semantics, so this is added as a genuine dependency, not a discipline exception. Requires a real Redis-compatible server (REDIS_URL) to do anything — see src/common/queue.module.ts, which falls back to a no-op queue (exactly like PG_POOL falls back to in-memory stores) when REDIS_URL is unset, so the app still boots with zero configuration. `ioredis` is also required directly: found only by actually running the real Redis-gated tests — bullmq@6 treats ioredis as an optional peer dependency it loads dynamically, not a bundled one, so `npm install bullmq` alone compiles fine but throws at runtime the first time a Queue/Worker actually tries to connect.
notes.nodemailer_is_a_real_dependency_not_a_st: Added 2026-09-11 for self-serve tenant signup's email-verification step (see tenant.service.ts/email.service.ts). Same reasoning as bullmq above, not jwt/totp/password: hand-rolling raw SMTP over `tls.connect()` (or AWS SigV4-signed HTTP calls to skip SMTP entirely) is a real reliability risk for production mail delivery — MIME encoding, TLS negotiation quirks, and provider-specific error handling are exactly the kind of thing a maintained library exists to get right, unlike JWT's fully self-contained ~100-line algorithm. Sends via AWS SES's SMTP interface (reusing the AWS account this project's Terraform already provisions RDS/ElastiCache under, rather than a new vendor) — see email.service.ts, which falls back to a console-logging stub (exactly like WhatsAppCloudApiService/NotYetVerifiedWhatsAppService) when SES_SMTP_HOST/SES_SMTP_USERNAME/SES_SMTP_PASSWORD aren't set, so self-serve signup is still fully testable with zero configuration.
notes.multer_override_2026-09-12: @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 pins its own bundled multer to 2.2.0, which `npm audit` (run while wiring up real image uploads for Catalog/Deals) flagged with 4 real high-severity advisories (DoS via crafted multipart field names, a file-descriptor leak on aborted uploads, a fileFilter race condition bypassing the size limit, and a DoS via oversized array-index field names) — all filed against <=2.2.0 specifically. multer@2.3.0 exists on the registry and isn't in any of those advisories' affected ranges, but NestJS hasn't bumped its own pin yet, so this `overrides` block forces 2.3.0 across the whole tree without waiting on that. Verified after adding it: `npm audit` reports zero vulnerabilities again, and the real upload flow (see catalog-item.service.ts/deal.service.ts's own image-upload endpoints) was live-tested against this forced version, not the vulnerable one.
